shots.intent: Open with curiosity while immediately separating a potentially useful game mechanic from medicine.
label_requirements: On-screen title: "Steam Is Not a Pharmacy"
Do not label Tetris as a treatment or therapy
If branded Tetris footage is used, identify it accurately and clear usage rights

shots.intent: Visualize a game engaging a particular cognitive system at a time-sensitive moment without implying that the game itself is medicine.
source_priority: Generated illustration of puzzle blocks engaging a visuospatial grid
label_requirements: On-screen contrast: "Possible mechanism ≠ medicine"
Avoid medical packaging, prescription symbols, or cure imagery around the game

shots.intent: Establish that the reported finding comes from controlled, protocol-specific trauma research rather than ordinary gameplay.
source_priority: Verified primary randomized controlled study figures or protocol diagrams
Custom protocol diagram based on verified study methods
label_requirements: Persistent qualifier: "Controlled, protocol-specific studies"
Outcome label: "Reported outcome: fewer intrusive memories"
Include compact source citation with author, year, and journal once verified
Do not show fabricated paper titles, statistics, effect sizes, or participant counts

shots.intent: Explain visuospatial interference as a proposed mechanism while preserving uncertainty and avoiding imagery of memory erasure.
label_requirements: On-screen label: "Proposed mechanism: visuospatial interference"
Secondary label: "Plausible, not settled"
Depict competing visual tasks, not deletion or destruction of a traumatic memory

shots.intent: Deliver the central scope boundary with an unmistakable visual correction.
source_priority: Original host footage with graphic overlays
label_requirements: Large text: "Fewer intrusions ≠ preventing PTSD"
Follow with: "Ordinary play ≠ the protocol"
Do not use a PTSD diagnosis disappearing, a cure badge, or before-and-after patient imagery

shots.intent: Reframe a commercial game storefront as a catalog of mechanics that researchers might screen, not as a digital pharmacy.
source_priority: Licensed or fair-use-limited Steam interface capture
label_requirements: On-screen heading: "Screening library"
Cross out or reject the label "Pharmacy"
If the Steam interface or logo appears, label it as a commercial storefront and avoid implying endorsement

shots.intent: Show the range of functions repeatedly demanded inside games without claiming improvement outside the game.
label_requirements: Sequential labels: "Attention", "Planning", "Spatial processing", "Coordination", "Goal pursuit"
Persistent qualifier: "Demands during play"
Avoid labels such as "trains," "improves," "rehabilitates," or "treats"

shots.intent: Convert gameplay observations into a research funnel that ends in testing rather than a therapy claim.
source_priority: Original conceptual chart based on the proposed framework
label_requirements: Flow labels: "Commercial game → mechanic → candidate function → hypothesis → controlled test"
End card within chart: "Hypotheses—not therapies"
Label the chart as a "Proposed research framework," not an empirical result

shots.intent: Make the near-transfer problem memorable by showing mastery that remains trapped inside the game.
source_priority: Host demonstration with a game controller
label_requirements: On-screen text: "Better at the game may mean only better at the game"
Do not imply that players are unintelligent or dysfunctional
Avoid presenting the visual as measured evidence

shots.intent: Surface self-selection and lack of transfer as core methodological problems.
source_priority: Verified longitudinal or controlled-study methodology graphic
label_requirements: Labels: "Self-selection", "Confounding", "Near transfer", "Daily function?"
Use a question mark for transfer to real-world outcomes
Do not portray player-group differences as causal effects

shots.intent: Balance possible benefits against concrete categories of harm without sensationalizing them.
label_requirements: Sequential labels: "Sleep loss", "Compulsion", "Toxicity", "Avoidance"
Frame these as potential harms, not inevitable effects
Avoid diagnostic labels or depictions of identifiable distressed individuals without consent

shots.intent: Present the required research sequence as a rigorous checklist that must precede any medical claim.
label_requirements: Reveal in narration order: "1. Isolate the mechanic"; "2. Use active controls"; "3. Measure symptoms + daily function"; "4. Track harms"; "5. Then make a medical claim"
Emphasize "Then—and only then" before the final step
Do not display approval seals, clinical efficacy badges, or regulatory symbols

shots.intent: Close by returning to the pharmacy metaphor and locking in the thesis that commercial games are candidates for discovery, not established medicine.
label_requirements: Final text: "Discovery library, not medicine"
Optional subline: "Clinical claims require controlled evidence"
Keep the commercial game on the library side of the visual, not inside a prescription bottle or pharmacy shelf
